Vector Index Basics Example

The vector index of DataReel 7.4, step by step: element types, exact and graph search, metrics, tags, changes, transactions and the format fields.

Contents

What It Shows
Running It
Sample Output
Source

What It Shows

The vector index (gxvindex.h) keeps vectors in a .vix file built on gxDatabase, with an HNSW graph for fast approximate search:

  1. The same 4,000 clustered vectors (dimension 32) in three files, one per element type: float32, float16 and int8 (signed bytes and a scale per vector). Their sizes show what each type costs.
  2. Exact() against Search(): the share of the exact 10 nearest the graph search finds (recall) and the time, for three search widths (ef).
  3. The three metrics on four 2-D points: l2 (squared distance), cosine (the vectors kept at unit length) and ip (inner product, largest first).
  4. Tags and a gxvFilter: tag 0 holds a category and tag 2 a day (yyyymmdd); a search keeps one category in two days.
  5. Update(), Delete() (a tombstone: Count() and Deleted()), Repair() (the graph made again from the live nodes) and Verify().
  6. The index's file attached to a gxdJournal: a transaction rolled back, then Reload() so the nodes in memory match the restored file.
  7. The phase D format fields (required and optional feature bits, codec, graph layout, the range of tag 2) and the logical digest: the same nodes inserted in another order give another graph and the same digest.

Running It

vector_basics [WORK_FOLDER]

The files go in the work folder (vector_basics_work by default). Each step prints its numbers and its checks; the exit code is 0 when every check passes.

Sample Output

1. 4000 vectors of dimension 32, three element types
  float32     441 ms to build, 1907904 bytes, 432 bytes a node (128 of them the vector)
  float16     596 ms to build, 1651904 bytes, 368 bytes a node (64 of them the vector)
  int8        522 ms to build, 1539904 bytes, 340 bytes a node (36 of them the vector)
2. Exact() against Search() (float32), 100 queries, recall@10
  exact:      9.0 ms
  ef  16:     8.4 ms, recall 1.000
  ef  64:     9.2 ms, recall 1.000
  ef 200:     8.5 ms, recall 1.000
  ok   the graph search finds at least 95% of the exact top 10 at the widest ef
3. Metrics on four 2-D vectors, query (1, 0)
  l2      order: 0 (0.000) 3 (0.580) 2 (2.000) 1 (81.000)
  ok   l2: the nearest point is (1, 0)
  cosine  order: 0 (0.000) 1 (0.000) 3 (0.293) 2 (1.000)
  ok   cosine: (1, 0) and (10, 0) are the same direction
  ip      order: 1 (-10.000) 0 (-1.000) 3 (-0.700) 2 (-0.000)
  ok   ip: (10, 0) has the largest inner product
4. A filter: category 1, days 2026-11-11 to 2026-11-12
  10 results, first id 7 (category 1, day 20261112)
  ok   every result is category 1 in the two days
5. Update, Delete, Repair and Verify
  live 3900, deleted 101
  ok   a deleted id is gone, an updated one is there
  ok   Repair() makes the graph again from the live nodes
  ok   Verify() finds no problem
6. A gxdJournal transaction rolled back, then Reload()
  in the transaction: 4010 live
  after Rollback() and Reload(): 4000 live
  ok   the rolled back inserts are gone
7. Format fields (phase D)
  required 0x0, optional 0x1, codec 0, graph layout 0, tag 2 range 20261110..20261114
  ok   the file keeps the range of tag 2 (a set can skip it)
  logical digest c5d420944975724c (4000 nodes), reverse order c5d420944975724c (4000 nodes)
  ok   the same nodes give the same logical digest, whatever the graph
All checks pass

From a 64-bit Linux build. The times differ from machine to machine and run to run; the checks, counts and digests do not.

Source

examples/oodb/vector_basics.cpp, one source file built by examples/CMakeLists.txt as vector_basics and run by tests/run_tests.sh. The comment at the top of the file describes each step. Back to the example programs.
